params.body:
Nightwatch #18 came back this morning at 08:15, for Ilse, twice in a day:

```
Cannot modify header information - headers already sent by
  app/Http/Controllers/Settings/RequirementsController.php:78
```

The title still says `CarpassController`, because Nightwatch groups on the message and the message is identical. So the second fault arrived carrying my "resolved" comment from the first one, written on 20 September.

## What it is

```php
header('Content-Type: application/octet-stream');
header("Content-disposition: attachment; filename=...");
echo Storage::disk('requirements')->get(base64_decode($url));
```

The bytes leave before Laravel builds its own response, and that response then tries to set headers on a body that is already gone. Worse than it sounds: anything that throws after the first byte lands there too, and `Storage::get()` throws on a file that is not in the bucket. So a missing file became a broken page instead of "this file is gone".

This is exactly the Car-Pass pdf fault of 20 September (R S3-4.2), in a different file.

## So this fixes the shape

Three places still answered that way: the requirements, the useful links, and the XML export of the own stock. All three return a response now, and the two file downloads answer 404 when the file is not in the bucket.

`ADownloadIsAnAnswerTest` reads every controller and fails on a bare `header()`, `echo`, `print`, `readfile` or `fpassthru`, with a second test that the three methods do return something, so the first one cannot go green because a method stopped doing anything at all.

## Verified

294 tests and 611 assertions across the rule catalogue, the smoke tests and the two new ones; `phpstan` green over the whole project; `pint` green on the added file.

Fixes bevinding een-download-is-een-antwoord.
params.title: A download is an answer, not output written straight out
